sources.title: Gavin R. G. Hambly, Gujarat, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Directly read political history, maritime trade and Persian cultural life. Formal assumption of sultan title in 1407 distinguished from earlier provincial independence. Do not adopt disputed Diu cession date.

sources.title: UNESCO, Historic City of Ahmadabad
sources.note: Directly read foundation in 1411, regional architectural craftsmanship and later residential heritage. No claim that every surviving pol house dates to the sultanate.

sources.title: UNESCO, Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
sources.note: Directly read conquest in 1484, capital development, 1536 abandonment and surviving pilgrimage landscape.

sources.title: Government of India, Champaner-Pavagadh World Heritage nomination
sources.note: Directly read archaeological synthesis of R. N. Mehta: printed pages 22-23, PDF pages 30-31, houses, roads and shops; printed page 32, PDF page 40, rainwater catchment, tanks and cleaning drains. Water landscape includes pre-sultanate works.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Textile Fragment, 30.112.36
sources.note: Direct object record: Gujarat, fifteenth-sixteenth century, cotton, block printing with mordant and resist, found at Fustat in Egypt.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Textile Fragment, 1978.546.51a
sources.note: Direct object record: probably Ahmedabad, fifteenth-sixteenth century; wax resist and indigo-dyed cotton, floral and geometric pattern.

sources.title: Cooper Union, Gender and Patronage, stepwell exhibition essay
sources.note: Directly read three-page scholarly exhibition essay, especially page 2, Rudabai, Bai Harir, water work and social space. Social description is a historical interpretation spanning periods, not a dated diary.

sources.title: M. A. Chaghatai, Muslim Monuments of Ahmadabad Through Their Inscriptions (1942), page 149
sources.note: Indexed primary PDF page 149, section XXVIII(c), line 5, gives the exact Sanskrit. Author states comparison with his own estampage, so this is an independent epigraphic study, not a mirror of Abbott. The short literal translation was also checked against Abbott, Epigraphia Indica IV, pages 299-300, visually read in downloaded original scan. Separate Arabic inscription on this page has a different date; no exact construction day inferred.

sources.title: Walters Art Museum, Two Kalpasutra folios, W.910
sources.note: Direct object record: Gujarat, about 1450, blue and gold, donors, monastic libraries, religious education and Paryushan use. Festival description is museum contextual explanation, not proof of a particular performance in 1492.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, The hidden drawings beneath Jain manuscript paintings
sources.note: Directly read conservation account by lead scientist Lucia Burgio: X-ray and infrared study with Yale, including late fifteenth-early sixteenth-century Gujarat manuscript leaf IS.46:50-1959.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, The arts of the Mughal empire
sources.note: Directly read Akbar’s Gujarat campaign, Surat in 1573 and Farrukh Beg’s later Akbarnama illustration, about 1590-1595, IS.2:117-1896. Shared URL with Mughal runtime card; cumulative budget checked.

proposedOverrides.name: Gujarat Sultanate
proposedOverrides.summary: A western Indian sultanate with oceanic trade, skilled textile workshops and ambitious water architecture.

batchIdentityNotes.association: One exact indexed record, no aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.interpretation: Western Indian Gujarat Sultanate under Mahmud I Begada, not the modern state. Formal sultan title in 1407; principal Mughal conquest 1572-1573, later Muzaffar III resistance. Imported short interval preserved as map coverage; no new geometry or implied exact historical frontier.
